topic.name: Type 2 Diabetes
objectives: Apply diagnostic criteria (fasting glucose, HbA1c, OGTT)
Initiate metformin and add second-line agents appropriately

lessons.title: 🍬 Type 2 Diabetes 101: The Insulin Resistance Epidemic

content_chunks.title: Why This Matters
content_chunks.content: Meet Maria: 52, BMI 34, family history of diabetes. Feels fine. Routine labs show fasting glucose 142 mg/dL. 'Must be a lab error,' she thinks. Repeat: 148. HbA1c: 7.2%. Maria has type 2 diabetes (T2DM) and didn't know it. She's one of 37 million Americans with diabetes (11% of population), and 1 in 5 don't know they have it. T2DM is the #1 cause of blindness, kidney failure, and non-traumatic amputations. Early detection + treatment prevents these complications!
content_chunks.visual_desc: Infographic: Glucose molecule → insulin resistance → complications tree (eyes, kidneys, nerves, heart, feet)

content_chunks.title: What IS Type 2 Diabetes?
content_chunks.content:
**Type 2 Diabetes**: Chronic metabolic disorder characterized by:
1. **Insulin resistance** - cells don't respond well to insulin
2. **Relative insulin deficiency** - pancreas can't keep up with demand
3. **Hyperglycemia** - persistently high blood glucose

**Pathophysiology**:
• Early: Pancreas compensates by making MORE insulin (hyperinsulinemia)
• Middle: Beta cells start to fail, insulin production drops
• Late: Severe insulin deficiency (may need insulin therapy)

**Risk Factors**:
• **Obesity** (80-90% of T2DM patients are overweight/obese)
• **Age** ≥45
• **Family history** (first-degree relative)
• **Sedentary lifestyle**
• **Race**: higher in Black, Hispanic, Native American, Asian, Pacific Islander
• **History of gestational diabetes**
• **PCOS** (polycystic ovarian syndrome)
• **Hypertension**, **dyslipidemia**, **CVD**
• **Prediabetes** (HbA1c 5.7-6.4%)
content_chunks.mnemonic: **T2DM Risk = FAMILY OB**: **F**amily history, **A**ge >45, **M**etabolic syndrome, **I**nactive lifestyle, **L**ipids abnormal, **Y**ears with prediabetes, **O**besity, **BP** elevated
content_chunks.visual_desc: Diagram: Insulin trying to unlock cell door, but lock is jammed (insulin resistance) → glucose piles up in bloodstream → high blood sugar

content_chunks.content: 🔥 **T2DM is often ASYMPTOMATIC for years!** Classic symptoms (polyuria, polydipsia, polyphagia, weight loss) appear late when glucose is VERY high (>200-300 mg/dL). This is why SCREENING is critical - most patients feel fine at diagnosis!

mnemonics.mnemonic: **T2DM Risk = FAMILY OB**: **F**amily history, **A**ge >45, **M**etabolic syndrome, **I**nactive lifestyle, **L**ipids abnormal, **Y**ears with prediabetes, **O**besity, **BP** elevated

quick_checks.q: Which is the PRIMARY defect in early Type 2 diabetes?
quick_checks.explanation: Early T2DM = INSULIN RESISTANCE (cells don't respond to insulin). Pancreas compensates by making more, but eventually can't keep up.

quick_checks.q: Most T2DM patients at diagnosis are:
quick_checks.explanation: Most T2DM patients are ASYMPTOMATIC at diagnosis! Found on routine screening. Classic symptoms appear late/severe.

content_chunks.title: Diagnostic Criteria (ADA 2023)
content_chunks.content:
**Diagnosis of DIABETES** (need ANY ONE of the following):

**1. HbA1c ≥6.5%**
• Reflects average glucose over 2-3 months
• CLIA-certified lab
• Repeat to confirm (unless symptomatic + glucose >200)

**2. Fasting Plasma Glucose (FPG) ≥126 mg/dL**
• Fasting = no calories for ≥8 hours
• Repeat to confirm

**3. 2-Hour OGTT ≥200 mg/dL**
• Oral glucose tolerance test (75g glucose load)
• Rarely used in adults (mainly pregnancy screening)

**4. Random glucose ≥200 mg/dL + symptoms**
• Symptoms: polyuria, polydipsia, unexplained weight loss
• No repeat needed if symptomatic

**PREDIABETES** (high risk, prevent progression!):
• HbA1c **5.7-6.4%**
• FPG **100-125 mg/dL** (impaired fasting glucose)
• 2-hr OGTT **140-199 mg/dL** (impaired glucose tolerance)

**NORMAL**:
• HbA1c <5.7%
• FPG <100 mg/dL
content_chunks.mnemonic: **Diabetes diagnosis = 6-1-2**: HbA1c ≥**6**.5%, Fasting ≥**1**26, **2**-hr OGTT ≥**200**, Random ≥**200** (with symptoms)
content_chunks.visual_desc: Three-zone diagram: GREEN (normal: HbA1c <5.7), YELLOW (prediabetes: 5.7-6.4), RED (diabetes: ≥6.5)

content_chunks.title: Who to Screen & When (USPSTF/ADA Guidelines)
content_chunks.content:
**Screen ALL adults** if:
• **Age 35-70** AND **overweight/obese** (BMI ≥25 or ≥23 in Asian Americans)
• OR **ANY age** if additional risk factors:
  - First-degree relative with diabetes
  - High-risk race/ethnicity (Black, Hispanic, Native American, Asian, Pacific Islander)
  - History of CVD
  - HTN (≥140/90 or on therapy)
  - HDL <35 or triglycerides >250
  - PCOS
  - Physical inactivity
  - History of gestational diabetes or baby >9 lbs

**How often?**
• If normal → rescreen every **3 years**
• If prediabetes → rescreen **yearly** + intensive lifestyle intervention!

**Preferred test**: **HbA1c** (convenient, no fasting) OR **fasting glucose**
content_chunks.visual_desc: Screening flowchart: Age 35-70 + overweight OR risk factors → Screen with HbA1c or FPG → Normal (rescreen q3y), Prediabetes (rescreen yearly + lifestyle), Diabetes (confirm + treat)

content_chunks.title: Prediabetes: The Last Warning!
content_chunks.content:
**Why it matters**: 5-10% of prediabetics progress to diabetes EACH YEAR. But progression is NOT inevitable!

**Treatment for Prediabetes**:

**1️⃣ Lifestyle Intervention** (FIRST-LINE - proven to work!)
• **Weight loss**: 7% of body weight (e.g., 14 lbs if 200 lbs)
• **Exercise**: 150 min/week moderate activity (brisk walking)
• **Diabetes Prevention Program (DPP)**: 58% reduction in diabetes risk!

**2️⃣ Metformin** (if high risk):
• Consider if: Age <60, BMI ≥35, history of gestational diabetes, or HbA1c rising toward 6.4%
• Metformin 850 mg BID (31% risk reduction in DPP trial)

**3️⃣ Monitor**: Recheck HbA1c yearly
content_chunks.clinical_pearl: Lifestyle modification (7% weight loss + 150 min/week exercise) is MORE effective than metformin for preventing diabetes (58% vs 31% risk reduction). Always start with lifestyle!

content_chunks.content: 🔥 **HbA1c can be FALSELY low** in: hemolytic anemia, recent blood loss, hemoglobinopathies (sickle cell), pregnancy, recent transfusion. **Falsely high** in: iron deficiency, B12 deficiency, uremia. If mismatch with glucose levels, use glucose-based criteria instead!

mnemonics.mnemonic: **Diabetes diagnosis = 6-1-2**: HbA1c ≥**6**.5%, Fasting ≥**1**26, **2**-hr OGTT ≥**200**, Random ≥**200** (with symptoms)

quick_checks.q: Patient has HbA1c 6.1%, fasting glucose 108 mg/dL. Diagnosis?
quick_checks.explanation: HbA1c 5.7-6.4% = PREDIABETES. FPG 100-125 also confirms prediabetes. Start intensive lifestyle intervention + yearly monitoring!

quick_checks.q: 40yo with BMI 32, fasting glucose 118 mg/dL. Next step?
quick_checks.explanation: FPG 100-125 = prediabetes. First-line is LIFESTYLE (7% weight loss + 150 min/week exercise). Metformin is second-line.

quick_checks.q: Which scenario does NOT require repeat testing to diagnose diabetes?
quick_checks.explanation: Random glucose ≥200 mg/dL WITH classic symptoms = diabetes, no repeat needed! All others need confirmation.

content_chunks.title: Treatment Goals (Individualize!)
content_chunks.content:
**HbA1c Goals** (ADA 2023):

**<7.0%** for MOST adults
• Newly diagnosed
• Long life expectancy
• No significant CVD
• Low hypoglycemia risk

**<6.5%** (more stringent) if:
• Short diabetes duration
• Can achieve without significant hypoglycemia
• No CVD

**<8.0%** (less stringent) if:
• History of severe hypoglycemia
• Limited life expectancy
• Advanced complications
• Extensive comorbidities
• Long-standing diabetes, hard to control

**Individualize** based on: patient preference, resources, support system, hypoglycemia risk

**Other goals**:
• **BP <130/80** (most diabetics)
• **LDL <100 mg/dL** (or <70 if ASCVD)
• **Statin** for primary prevention if age >40 OR other ASCVD risk factors
content_chunks.visual_desc: Target dartboard: Bullseye (HbA1c <6.5%), middle ring (<7%), outer ring (<8%), with patient factors determining which target to aim for

content_chunks.title: Step 1: Lifestyle + Metformin
content_chunks.content:
**Lifestyle Modifications** (start at diagnosis!):
• **Weight loss**: 5-10% (if overweight)
• **Exercise**: 150 min/week moderate + 2 days resistance training
• **Mediterranean or DASH diet**
• **Limit refined carbs/added sugars**
• **Diabetes self-management education (DSME)**

**METFORMIN** = **FIRST-LINE medication** (unless contraindicated)

**Why metformin?**
• ↓ hepatic glucose production
• ↑ insulin sensitivity
• **Weight neutral** or modest weight loss
• **No hypoglycemia** (doesn't increase insulin)
• **Cheap**
• Proven CV benefits

**Dosing**:
• Start **500 mg PO daily or BID** with meals
• Titrate up every 1-2 weeks
• Target: **2000 mg/day** (divided BID) - max 2550 mg
• Use **extended-release (ER)** if GI intolerance

**Side Effects**:
• **GI upset** (50%): nausea, diarrhea, cramping (improves over weeks - start low, go slow!)
• **Vitamin B12 deficiency** (long-term): check B12 yearly
• **Lactic acidosis** (RARE): avoid if eGFR <30

**Contraindications**:
• eGFR <30 mL/min (stop if <30, be cautious if 30-45)
• Severe liver disease
• Acute illness (hold during hospitalization for surgery, contrast studies)
content_chunks.visual_desc: Metformin mechanism diagram: blocks liver glucose production (gluconeogenesis) + increases muscle glucose uptake

content_chunks.title: Step 2: Adding Second-Line Agents
content_chunks.content:
**When?** If HbA1c not at goal after 3 months on metformin + lifestyle

**CHOOSING THE NEXT MED** (depends on patient factors):

**IF ASCVD or high CV risk** → **GLP-1 RA** or **SGLT2i** (proven CV benefit!)

**IF Heart Failure or CKD** → **SGLT2i** (proven benefit!)

**IF Main goal is weight loss** → **GLP-1 RA** (best for weight!)

**IF Cost is major concern** → **Sulfonylurea** (cheap but causes hypoglycemia)

---

**GLP-1 Receptor Agonists** (incretin mimetics)
• **Examples**: semaglutide (Ozempic, weekly), dulaglutide (Trulicity, weekly), liraglutide (Victoza, daily)
• **Mechanism**: ↑ insulin, ↓ glucagon, ↓ appetite, slow gastric emptying
• **Benefits**: 
  - **Weight loss 5-15 lbs** (semaglutide up to 15%!)
  - **CV benefit** (↓ MACE in high-risk patients)
• **Side effects**: Nausea (common initially), diarrhea, pancreatitis (rare)
• **Avoid**: Personal/family history of medullary thyroid cancer or MEN 2
• **Route**: Subcutaneous injection (once weekly preferred)

**SGLT2 Inhibitors** (gliflozins)
• **Examples**: empagliflozin (Jardiance), dapagliflozin (Farxiga), canagliflozin (Invokana)
• **Mechanism**: Block glucose reabsorption in kidney → pee out glucose!
• **Benefits**:
  - **CV benefit** (↓ MACE, ↓ HF hospitalization)
  - **Renal protection** (↓ CKD progression)
  - **Weight loss** 5-10 lbs
  - **BP reduction** (diuretic effect)
• **Side effects**: Genital yeast infections (10%), UTIs, DKA (rare but serious!), Fournier's gangrene (very rare)
• **Avoid**: eGFR <30 (or <45 for some)

**Sulfonylureas** (older, cheap)
• **Examples**: glipizide, glyburide, glimepiride
• **Mechanism**: ↑ insulin secretion from pancreas
• **Benefits**: Cheap, effective (↓ HbA1c ~1.5%)
• **Side effects**: **HYPOGLYCEMIA** (major risk!), weight gain
• **Avoid**: Elderly, erratic eating, renal/hepatic impairment

**DPP-4 Inhibitors** (gliptins)
• **Examples**: sitagliptin (Januvia), linagliptin (Tradjenta)
• **Mechanism**: ↑ GLP-1 (prevents its breakdown)
• **Benefits**: Weight neutral, no hypoglycemia, oral
• **Cons**: Modest HbA1c reduction (~0.5-0.8%), expensive, no CV benefit

**Insulin**
• Reserve for: HbA1c >10%, symptomatic hyperglycemia, pregnancy, T1DM
• Start with basal insulin (glargine, detemir) at bedtime
• Titrate based on fasting glucose
content_chunks.visual_desc: Decision tree: If ASCVD/HF/CKD → SGLT2i or GLP-1. If weight loss priority → GLP-1. If cost priority → sulfonylurea. All stay on metformin!

content_chunks.content: 🔥 **Don't wait to intensify!** If HbA1c not at goal after 3 months, ADD another agent (don't just increase metformin dose if already at 2000 mg). 'Clinical inertia' (waiting too long to adjust) is a huge problem in diabetes care!

mnemonics.mnemonic: **Metformin eGFR: 30 is the line** (stop if <30, caution if 30-45)

mnemonics.trigger: Second-line diabetes meds with CV benefit
mnemonics.mnemonic: **Heart loves SGLT-GLP**: **SGLT2i** and **GLP-1 RA** have proven CV benefit!

quick_checks.q: Newly diagnosed T2DM, HbA1c 7.8%, BMI 31, no CVD. First medication?
quick_checks.explanation: METFORMIN is first-line for nearly all T2DM patients (unless contraindicated). Start with lifestyle + metformin!

quick_checks.q: T2DM on metformin, HbA1c still 8.2%, has heart failure. Best add-on?
quick_checks.explanation: SGLT2 inhibitors have PROVEN benefit in heart failure (↓ HF hospitalization). Best choice for diabetic with HF!

quick_checks.q: Why is metformin contraindicated in eGFR <30?
quick_checks.explanation: Metformin accumulates with poor renal function → risk of LACTIC ACIDOSIS (rare but life-threatening). Stop if eGFR <30.
